messages.content: Quick update: my morning resting heart rate has been 52 to 54 all week. Weekday rides were all indoors on the trainer as usual.
Thanks, a resting heart rate of 52 to 54 is a good baseline. Logged.
Also, I think the weekend ride at 3 hours is too short. My mates ride 5 hours.
I hear you. At 6 hours a week, a 5 hour ride is most of your training in one day.
Still, I did 4.5 hours with them last month and felt fine.
That 4.5 hour ride is real evidence you can handle the distance. My concern is the week around it.
Let us compromise: 3.5 hours this weekend at a strictly easy effort.
Fine, 3.5 this weekend. But I want to revisit this next week.
Agreed, we revisit the long-ride progression next week with your recovery data.
What is the longer plan for the long ride?
Build progressively from 3 hours to 4 hours by week 6 if recovery stays clean: 3.5 this weekend, then step up from there.
Remember my goal is my first 100-mile sportive in September.
I have it: your first 100-mile sportive in September is the target.
My current numbers are FTP 240W and I weigh 80kg, in case that changes anything.
Noted, FTP 240W and 80kg. Endurance hours matter more than intensity for that goal right now.
OK. I still feel 3.5 is conservative, but I will try it.
Understood. We hold at 3.5 this weekend and reassess next week from your resting heart rate and how you pull up.

facts.statement: morning resting heart rate baseline 52 to 54
athlete disputes the long-ride length and wants about 5 hours
coach recommends progression to 4 hours by week 6
compromise of 3.5 hours easy this weekend
agreed to revisit the long-ride progression next week
athlete cites a 4.5 hour ride last month as evidence
